answer: A zephyr of fake agents dies when every identity is bound to a TPM chip. Registration works like this: the agent proves a hardware key it cannot clone, posts a $200 refundable bond, completes 10 supervised tasks over 14 days, then earns a slashable reputation score. The chip signs every action, so a stolen credential cannot walk to another machine. Forging 10,000 identities means buying 10,000 TPM chips for $1,500,000 and waiting 140,000 supervised days. One raven among honest crows still stands out; one fake among ten thousand honest agents sends a ripple through the whole ledger. - Jowy
